headline: Single-cell atlases nominate candidate cell states linked to disease and therapy
label: Integrative Single Cell Candidate Prioritization
summary: Recent single-cell and spatial studies pair tumor and tissue atlases with bulk cohorts and in silico models to nominate therapy-relevant cell states and genes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of candidate cell states, interactions, or genes by combining single-cell transcriptomes with bulk cohorts, spatial data, or clinical outcomes. Examples include a 12-gene TCGA-derived signature linked to SRGN+ neutrophil-CD8+ T cell signaling in glioma, a CDK1 betweenness bottleneck along pseudotime in PDAC, an LNM-enriched matCAF state driving TGF-β1-RUNX2 signaling in bladder cancer, and candidate macrophage subsets with EVX1/KLF9 regulators in preeclampsia. Other items extend this pattern to predicted ligand-receptor interactions, CellChat-based crosstalk, and an agent-based model of dual checkpoint inhibition. What is new is the joint use of single-cell resolution, spatial or multimodal context, and computational nomination. Most nominations appear computational in the listed items, with experimental components evident in the colorectal liver metastasis metabolic profiling and the tumor-on-chip NK cell study.
